Climate and Evolution: Will We Survive the Future? - Historian Naomi OreskesLa Jolla, CA. (5-15-2015) 19 Min.

[linked to start of talk] Description:

Renowned historian of science Naomi Oreskes of Harvard University addresses the question of human impacts on climate and whether we will survive the future, and posits that humanity will need to make substantial change in what we do and how we think.

No problem. I thought Oreskes call for the scientific community to speak out regardless of the political consequences was particularly poignant. Although the IPCC reports are given a lot of deference in the press, what isn't well understood by most is that the IPCC is a consensus body. So it's very conservative by nature as all the member nations have to sign off on the published reports. That includes Saudi Arabia and other OPEC nations—which on the surface at least appears to be a pretty glaring conflict of interest as the consequences of the reports and subsequent actions will directly affect their biggest source of revenue. These reports put those that find and publish alarming findings more in a position of being whistle blowers, which is not an easy career path, and over time it's increasingly clear the alarmists are closer to predicting what is actually unfolding. Although, as in all matters, some are likely off the deep end.
The trail of forms fades into the darkness.
You wake to see Earth slowly floating away, ethereal forms left in its wake. Realization strikes, you're dead.

Your eyes dart around, panicked. Where does this leave you? Are you now stuck in space forever? A terror ten times that of being in the open, empty ocean washes over you.

Then you see it. You never before noticed from beneath the atmosphere how colorful the stars are. Your fear slowly recedes like an ebbing wave across your feet, replaced instead by awe.

As you gaze more observantly at your surroundings, you notice the swirling ethereal forms heading toward you.

My vision fades, the periphery of my sight goes first, and darkness flows closer to the center until I see no more. Memories so vivid appear in the blackness. My life appears before me, almost as a dream. Memories of my life that I had not remembered are finally being realized. Every fine detail of the scene is present. What I thought was forgotten, has now come back to me in a form so authentic. They said your life flashes before your eyes when you die, is this what this is? I watch my life pass by. I feel everything I felt before, but in such a clear form it was hard to believe that this was but a memory. I also feel regret for what I wish I had done, and pride for what I accomplished. I am seeing my life from all perspectives. Who would have known death would be so lucid? I am no longer mortal, despite experiencing death. Words can not describe experiences of such clarity and emotion. As my life ends again in my memory, I fade back to seeing the world slowly drifting away, but I can feel something behind me. It is a light with a certain warmth and comfort to it. Now the fabled light one sees as they day has manifested before me. I drift towards it, until it is all I see. The light will consume me, and I soon will enter the next phase of my afterlife. Heaven? Hell? Rebirth? Soon I will know.
What else is there to do but drift off and remember the cosmic opera we once called life?
